drafts.title: Florida Oct 1: utilities must file large-load tariffs so 50 MW+ customers pay their own way.
drafts.window: Tuesday ~7 PM MT hottest, or secondary ~2-3 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Florida Statute 366.043 (from SB 484) requires every public electric utility to file a large-load tariff with the Florida PSC no later than October 1, 2026. Trigger: customer with anticipated monthly peak of 50 MW or more at a single location. Law says that customer bears full cost of service (connection, incremental transmission/generation, O&M) and nonpayment risk must not land on the general body of ratepayers. Tools allowed: CIAC, demand charges, take-or-pay, minimum contract terms, early exit fees, collateral. Soft-pedal Senate Ratepayer and Pacific Power Oregon Mon twins as the only story. Kitchen-table: Florida put a calendar date on who pays. Ask YOUR PSC what date you have.
bullets: Fla. Stat. 366.043(8): each public utility shall file a complying large-load tariff for commission approval no later than October 1, 2026.
Large-load customer defined as anticipated monthly peak load of 50 MW or more (highest average load over a 15-minute interval) at a single location; load-splitting to dodge the class is banned.

Tariff must reasonably ensure the large-load customer bears its own full cost of service and that cost is not shifted to the general body of ratepayers; risk of nonpayment may not be borne by households.

Commission may approve tools including contributions in aid of construction, minimum demand charges, financial guarantees, take-or-pay / contracted capacity payments, minimum period of service, early termination fees.
Signed into law May 2026 (SB 484 / Ch. 2026-65 era); Clean Energy Group summarizes Florida among states creating separate large-load tariffs. Soft-pedal campaign labels.
drafts.body:
Florida just put a date on the kitchen table.

By October 1, every big Florida electric utility has to file a large-load tariff with the state commission. The law defines a large load as about 50 megawatts of peak at one site. That is data-center and heavy industrial territory, not your dishwasher. The rule is plain: those customers are supposed to cover their own wires, substations, and generation add-ons. Households are not supposed to eat the nonpayment risk if a campus walks away.

Soft-pedal Senate scorekeeping. Soft-pedal Oregon Schedule 401 as a twin. Soft-pedal party labels. The useful sticky note is the calendar.

Sticky notes for a 45-year-old homeowner near a proposed campus, or a 62-year-old on a fixed income:

1) Search your state PSC / PUC site for "large load" or "50 MW" or "data center tariff."
2) Write down Florida's October 1 filing deadline. Ask what YOUR state's deadline is, if any.
3) Soft-pedal "Congress already fixed my bill." A House vote is not a Florida tariff filing.
4) Ask whether take-or-pay, collateral, and exit fees are in the draft tariff.
5) If a campus files near you, ask who funds the substation before dirt moves.

35-54 line: Premium saves "Florida Oct 1 / 50 MW / households not the bagholders."

55+ line: independence is a bill that does not quietly fund someone else's server farm.

drafts.title: Massachusetts heat pump winter rates: Nov 1 deeper discounts; ~$16-$21/mo more for many.
drafts.window: Tuesday ~7 PM MT hottest, or secondary ~2-3 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Canary Media Sep 17, 2026: Massachusetts DPU approved even lower winter heat-pump rates for National Grid and Unitil starting Nov 1 (Eversource already cut transmission). More than 65,000 households. Last winter the program saved residents more than $37 million total. New transmission cuts: National Grid from about $0.055/kWh to $0.02; Unitil from about $0.042 to $0.015. At 600 kWh/month, about $16-$21 extra monthly savings on top of existing discounts; Switchbox: National Grid + Unitil customers stand to save an additional ~$9.8 million this winter vs last. Eversource page: average enrollee paid about $430 less last winter (~$72/mo). Only state requiring major utilities to offer heat-pump seasonal rates. Soft-pedal climate sermon. Kitchen-table: if you heat with a heat pump, check your utility rate code before Nov 1.
bullets: MA regulators approved National Grid and Unitil deeper winter heat-pump rates effective Nov 1, 2026 (Canary Media Sep 17, 2026); season runs Nov 1 through April 30.
More than 65,000 Massachusetts households on heat-pump rates; last winter program saved residents more than $37 million total.
National Grid transmission portion for heat-pump rate: about $0.055/kWh down to $0.02; Unitil about $0.042 down to $0.015 (DPU-ordered to match Eversource approach).
At ~600 kWh/month, Canary cites about $16-$21/month additional bill drop vs prior discount math; Switchbox: ~$9.8M extra winter savings for Grid+Unitil cohort vs last year.
Eversource: customers enrolled paid about $430 less last winter heating season (~$72/month average); Mass Save rebate installs since 2019 often auto-enroll.
drafts.body:
Winter heat should not punish you for ditching the oil truck.

Massachusetts is still the only state that makes the big utilities offer a lower winter rate for homes with heat pumps. Last winter that program put more than $37 million back in household pockets across more than 65,000 homes. Now National Grid and Unitil just got approval to cut the winter rate even deeper starting November 1. On a 600 kilowatt-hour month, that deeper cut is on the order of $16 to $21 extra savings. Eversource says its average enrollee already paid about $430 less last winter.

Soft-pedal climate sermons. Soft-pedal battery VPP maps. Soft-pedal "free heat." This is a delivery-rate fix so you are not overcharged for wires when the grid is not peaking.

Sticky notes for a 48-year-old who just installed a heat pump, or a 65-year-old watching winter bills:

1) Call or click your utility and ask if you are on the heat-pump winter rate.
2) If you got a Mass Save rebate after 2019, check whether you auto-enrolled.
3) Write Nov 1 on the calendar. That is when the deeper Grid/Unitil rates start.
4) Soft-pedal "my summer bill will also drop." Summer is usually standard residential rates.
5) If you are outside Massachusetts, ask your PUC whether a heat-pump seasonal rate is even on the docket.

35-54 line: Premium saves "Nov 1 / 65k homes / $16-$21 extra / $430 last winter cite."

55+ line: a fair winter rate is independence when the furnace truck used to own you.

drafts.title: New Jersey A796: data centers on a large-load class; 85% take-or-pay for 10 years.
drafts.window: Tuesday ~7 PM MT hottest, or secondary ~2-3 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: NJ A-796/S-731 signed by Gov. Mikie Sherrill July 6, 2026 (NJ League of Municipalities). Utilities must file a large-load data-center tariff with the BPU. Threshold: board sets MW size not greater than 50 MW; statute text also references 100 MW peak for "large load data center" definition in the municipal summary. Key household guardrail: new large-load data-center customer must provide financial guarantees to take at least 85% of service requested for not less than 10 years. Costs attributable to those customers allocated to them, not to other ratepayers. Clean Energy Group notes a first-of-its-kind path for data centers to help fund household efficiency upgrades to free grid capacity. Soft-pedal Senate/Oregon/Florida twins as the only post. Kitchen-table: 85% for 10 years is the sticky note.
bullets: A-796/S-731 signed July 6, 2026; requires each NJ electric public utility to develop and submit a large-load data-center tariff to the BPU (NJLM July 8, 2026 readout).
BPU standards: MW size designation not greater than 50 MW; aggregate commonly owned/contiguous sites so no project splitting; other customers must not subsidize large data-center customers.
Financial guarantee authority: new large-load data-center customer provides adequate guarantees they will take at least 85% of service requested for not less than 10 years from service commencement.
Tariff petitions due no later than 180 days after BPU issues standards order; tariffs apply beginning one year after enactment as approved.
Clean Energy Group: NJ measure includes incentive path for data centers to secure capacity by paying for household efficiency upgrades elsewhere on the grid.
drafts.body:
New Jersey put a number on the handshake.

If a data center wants a big slice of the grid, the new law says the Board of Public Utilities can make them guarantee they will take at least 85 percent of the power they ask for, for at least 10 years. Utilities have to file a special large-load tariff so those costs do not slide onto everyone else's bill. The threshold talk sits around 50 megawatts, with rules against splitting a campus into cute little meters to dodge the class.

Soft-pedal Florida Oct 1 as a twin-only post. Soft-pedal Senate drama. Soft-pedal Oregon Schedule 401 as the only comparison. The kitchen-table piece is the guarantee.

Sticky notes for a 42-year-old in North Jersey, or a 60-year-old watching PJM capacity costs:

1) Search NJ BPU for "large load data center" tariff dockets.
2) Write "85% for 10 years" on a sticky note. Ask if YOUR state has anything like it.
3) Soft-pedal "my bill already dropped." Tariffs take months to write and approve.
4) Ask whether efficiency-for-capacity deals show up as real household programs, not slogans.
5) Soft-pedal company drama. Keep the who-pays frame.

35-54 line: Premium saves "NJ 85% take-or-pay / 10 years / not your subsidy."

55+ line: long contracts are how you keep stranded costs off a fixed income.

drafts.title: Dominion Virginia GS-5: data centers on 14-year contracts; pay 85% of wires costs.
drafts.window: Tuesday ~7 PM MT hottest, or secondary ~2-3 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Virginia SCC fact sheet (posted Feb 24, 2026) on Dominion Energy Virginia GS-5 large-load class: separate rates so data centers pay unique costs and avoid cost shifting. New large-load customers contracting on or after January 1, 2027 take and pay for electric service at least 14 years. Minimum charges: pay at least 85% of transmission and distribution costs each month regardless of actual use (existing large loads too, with pre-2016 exemption). Collateral: up to 60% of minimum charges over the contract for new customers from Jan 1, 2027. Soft-pedal Google+Georgia Power LIVE and Senate Mon twin. Kitchen-table: Virginia already wrote the contract length into the rate case.
bullets: VA SCC: Dominion GS-5 is a separate rate class for large-load / hyperscale data-center customers so rates recover unique costs and minimize shifting (SCC Data Center Initiatives fact sheet, Case PUR-2025-00058).
Minimum contract obligation: take and pay for electric service for at least 14 years; applies to new large-load customers who contract on or after January 1, 2027.

Minimum charges: pay at least 85% of transmission and distribution costs incurred to serve them each month, regardless of electricity actually used; applies to new and existing large loads (customers who began service before Jan 1, 2016 exempt).
Collateral: large-load customers without sufficient credit may guarantee up to 60% of minimum charges over the contract term (new customers from Jan 1, 2027).
SCC also ordered Dominion to submit interconnection process for large loads for review; alternative cost-allocation proposals required in future cases.
drafts.body:
Virginia is Data Center Alley. The state commission already put data centers in their own rate class.

Dominion's GS-5 class is built so big loads pay for the unique costs of serving them. New contracts on or after January 1, 2027 carry at least a 14-year take-and-pay obligation. Every month those customers owe at least 85 percent of the transmission and distribution costs built for them, even if they use less juice that month. Weak credit can mean collateral covering up to 60 percent of those minimum charges.

Soft-pedal Google+Georgia Power LIVE. Soft-pedal Kairos LIVE. Soft-pedal Senate scorekeeping as the only news. This is a real tariff wall in the state that hosts the densest campuses.

Sticky notes for a 50-year-old in Northern Virginia, or a 64-year-old anywhere watching AI load headlines:

1) Search your utility for a large-load or "GS-5 style" class.
2) Write "14 years" and "85% of wires costs" on a sticky note.
3) Soft-pedal "my residential rate already fell." Ask for the order, not the press release.
4) Compare Virginia's 14-year floor to New Jersey's 10-year / 85% take-or-pay and Florida's Oct 1 filings.
5) If a campus files near you, ask who posts the collateral before the substation is built.

35-54 line: Premium saves "Virginia GS-5 / 14 years / 85% T&D / Jan 2027."

55+ line: long contracts and collateral are how you keep stranded wires off a Social Security budget.

drafts.title: CAFE Sep 28: fleet mpg target 34.9 by 2031; kitchen-table play is still home charge.
drafts.window: Tuesday ~7 PM MT hottest, or secondary ~2-3 PM MT. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Sep 28, 2026: U.S. DOT / NHTSA finalized new CAFE rules. Fleet-wide target about 34.9 mpg by 2031, down from prior path toward about 50.4 mpg (Detroit Free Press / admin readout). Transportation Secretary Duffy: ends what admin calls illegal EV mandate; claims average new-vehicle price about $1,300 lower. Soft politics. Soft climate sermon. Kitchen-table for first EV at 62: whatever Washington does to fleet averages, YOUR weekly miles still win or lose on home $/kWh vs pump $/gal. Do not invent pump prices. Point readers to compare their own numbers. Soft-pedal Manheim used-EV and lease ladders.
bullets: Final rule announced Sep 28, 2026: fleet-wide average about 34.9 mpg for passenger cars and light trucks by model year 2031 (Detroit Free Press Sep 28, 2026).
Prior Biden-era path cited about 50.4 mpg by 2031; new path cited about 32.3 mpg in 2027 rising to 34.9 mpg by 2031.
Admin / Duffy claim: rule reduces average price of a new vehicle by about $1,300; auto-industry lobby said prior standards were out of step with market demand.
Rule also changes credit trading and some vehicle classification details; litigation expected. Soft-pedal court drama.
Kitchen-table constant: home charging economics still beat most public DC for weekly miles; soft-pedal "EVs are cancelled" hot takes.
drafts.body:
Washington just moved the mileage goalposts again.

On September 28 the Transportation Department finalized new fuel-economy rules. The fleet-wide target lands around 34.9 miles per gallon by 2031, down from a prior path near 50. Soft-pedal the campaign speeches on both sides. Soft-pedal the cable-news fight. One admin number worth writing down: they say the average new vehicle could cost about $1,300 less under the new path.

Here is the kitchen-table part that still belongs to you, not to a press secretary:

1) Your weekly miles still care about home cents per kilowatt-hour versus what you pay at the pump.
2) Soft-pedal "EVs are dead." Soft-pedal "gas is dead." Compare YOUR numbers on a sticky note.
3) Soft-pedal Manheim used-price tickers and lease ladders.
4) If you already drive electric, keep charging at home for the cheap miles and use retail DC for road trips.
5) If you are shopping your first EV at 60-plus, ask the dealer for the home-charge math before you argue about federal mpg averages.

35-54 line: Premium saves "34.9 mpg by 2031 / ~$1,300 sticker claim / still do your home $/kWh math."

55+ line: independence is knowing your own fuel math when the rulebook changes.
